body:
I'm writing this a couple of months after the actual experience and as a result, there is some blurring between this experience and two other experiences with acid that occurred around the same time.
Well, it was one of those days that I live for.  I had the entire house to myself (I was home from school for summer in a private and rural setting) and as always in that situation, I was very happy.  As irresponsible and anti-social as this may be, I enjoy taking drugs by myself.  There's something about being completely free of the self-consciousness that comes from being around others that I appreciate.
Anyway, I had decided the day before that I would do some acid.  I had taken one hit a few weeks earlier and then two a few days after that.   Two had been fairly strong, but I feel as though I didn't get the full effects that the world's most powerful psychedelic had to offer.  As a result, I decided to take four, two at first, then the next two roughly an hour later.  However, about 40 minutes into the trip (I was passing time by drawing in the sketchbook) my body was vibrating so badly that I felt I couldn't draw accurately anymore.  Slightly discouraged by my lack of motor skills, I decided to only take one more hit, totalling three.  Then, not being able to draw, I started writing, but I had difficulty seeing and reading what I was writing so I gave up.
I should mention that the whole day I had music playing.  I am quite sensitive to music and I was sure to create a playlist of happy music.
After writing, I realized I still had all three acid blotters in my mouth and my throat was feeling weird from swallowing so much (in a vain attempt to absorb all the acid I guess).  About this time, my jaw started to tense up too.  This wouldn't relent for the entire duration of the trip and was unpleasant, but by no means was this extreme.  All the while, my body was still twitching and vibrating and there was so much going on in my field of vision I felt like I could barely see any of what was going on.  I mean, I wasn't hallucinating, I was just trying to take in too many details at once.  I would hallucinate later on though.  The sky would become beautifully patterned and filled with spectrums and the pattern on the couch would flow like water, very Fear and Loathing is Las Vegasesque.  Also, whenever I would close my eyes I would see patterns dancing to the music.
As usual with more powerful drugs (I consider myself a fairly experienced user of psychedelics: peyote, salvia, mushrooms, dxm, lsa, and abundant use of codeine and opium), I became deeply introspective a couple of hours into the trip and the question that always seems to come up with acid, 'so when's the life changing experience going to happen'.  Whenever I start asking this question, I become disenchanted with being high.  I knew I needed to distract myself so I went outside.  I got inside a vehicle (I had enough common sense to know I couldn't drive) and pretended to drive...through a desert.  Eventually, doing this weirded me out so I started wandering through the woods surrounding my house.  My face started to stretch back, baring my teeth into a snarl.  I was in a weird state where I thought I was a dinosaur but I was still human and I was genuinely terrified.  I kept glancing over my shoulder because I thought people were watching me being a dinosaur.  I couldn't stop myself.
Anyway, now that I've got my delusions written and out of the way I can address the question I ran away from.  I feel as though all the literature I've read about acid has tricked me into thinking that acid will change your life, give you an entire new perspective of the world or spiritual epiphany.  I'm beginning to think this will never happen to me, and near the end of the trip, I began to realize this.  I don't need acid to change my life. It's fine the way it is, and the more I believe this, and the more I personally view acid as a purely recreational drug, the more I will appreciate acid.
Well, after reviewing what I wrote, it seems as though I want to justify my shallow use of drugs.  There's nothing wrong with trying something new just for the sake of it.
